max (eng-platform): Heads-up — we need a decision on how we surface routing fallthroughs to clients. Example: smart routing can't find a low-latency replica and we either fallback to a higher-latency model or a degraded config. Currently some endpoints return 200 + body warning, others return 429/503. We should be consistent.
alec (eng-runtime): Agreed. FWIW runtime currently treats two cases separately:\n- capacity_fallback: picks a compatible model variant (still 200) with a `warning` field\n- capacity_block: no compatible model available -> 503/Retry-After
kevin (devex): From client SDK POV mixing 200-with-warning vs 503 is confusing. SDKs want deterministic retry hints. If we keep 200 for fallbacks we need structured metadata in headers so SDKs can react similarly to a 5xx/429.
sophia (product): Important for console UX too — customers should understand whether traffic was served with a fallback (and cost/quality impact) vs throttled. We need signals in dashboard and billing telemetry.
max (eng-platform): Proposal: standardize on semantic HTTP mapping:\n- Hard block (no variant) -> 503 (service_unavailable) or 429 for quota-exhausted.\n- Soft fallback (served by alternate model/config) -> 200 with explicit `X-Redwood-Fallback` header + telemetry tags.
This keeps successful responses semantic but makes fallback machine-detectable.
alec (eng-runtime): That seems sensible. Can we also include a canonical `error_subcode` header for both 4xx/5xx and 200-fallback flows so logs and SDKs use same key? Example: `X-Redwood-Error: routing.fallthrough; subcode=region-sparse`.
kevin (devex): Yes, prefer single header name. SDK can then treat `status >= 500 || X-Redwood-Error` as retriable or special-case. Example client logic: `if (status >= 500 || headers['x-redwood-error']?.startsWith('retryable')) backoff()`.
sophia (product): UX ask: in the Console request details panel show a little banner when `X-Redwood-Fallback: yes` with model variant used and expected perf delta. Also link to rollout/feature flag that triggered fallback routing policy.
max (eng-platform): Telemetry keys proposal for tracing/logging: `error_class` (routing_fallback|capacity_block|quota_exhausted), `error_subcode` (region_sparse, model_shrink), `route_policy` (latency|cost|isolation), `fallback_model` (model-id). These should be emitted for both successful fallback responses and errors.
alec (eng-runtime): Implementation note: runtime can add headers and tags at the gateway level so we don't need model-serving changes for the initial rollout. Gateway sets `X-Redwood-Fallback: 1`, `X-Redwood-Error: routing.fallthrough;subcode=region_sparse`, and emits telemetry.
kevin (devex): For SDKs we should publish a small compat doc + sample code. Example header usage snippet:```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
X-Redwood-Fallback: 1
X-Redwood-Error: routing.fallthrough;subcode=region_sparse
X-Redwood-Hint: try-lower-temperature

{ "id": "...", "object": "text_completion", "choices": [...], "warning": "served by fallback-model: redwood-mini-v1 (expected latency +120ms)" }
```This lets SDKs show a warning and surface telemetry.
sophia (product): What's the plan for client-facing wording? We should avoid scary words like "error" in user-visible messages. Use "served by alternate model" + quality note and link to docs.
max (eng-platform): Agreed. Header `X-Redwood-Error` is internal/telemetry; for UX use `warning` text in body like `served_by: redwood-mini-v1; quality_impact: low` and console banner uses friendly copy: "Request routed to alternate model to maintain availability — slight quality difference expected." Keep copy short.
alec (eng-runtime): One more edge: rate limiting vs routing fallback. Quota should remain 429/Quota-Remaining semantics. If we want to enable soft serving under quota (e.g., overflow to cheaper pool) that's a separate policy with explicit header `X-Redwood-Quota-Mode: overflow`. Need product signoff.
sophia (product): I'm OK with overflow as an opt-in feature per customer. We'll treat it as an enterprise toggle; console needs to show actual cost delta and a consent flow.
kevin (devex): Action items:\n1) eng-runtime to add gateway headers + emit telemetry tags (owner: alec)\n2) eng-platform to add mapping doc and standard header names + SDK guidance (owner: max + kevin)\n3) product to draft user-friendly copy and console banner mock (owner: sophia)\n4) security/review if any header leaks PII (quick check)
max (eng-platform): I'll file a small RFC and attach examples. Leaving a checklist in RFC: header names, telemetry keys, SDK snippet, console banner copy, rollout gating. ETA for RFC PR: EOD tomorrow.
ci-bot: deploy-canary: gateway/v2 -> 1/3 nodes (success) :white_check_mark:
alec (eng-runtime): I'll start the gateway change branch and flag you in the PR, max.
kevin (devex): I'll prep a tiny SDK patch that treats `X-Redwood-Fallback` as metadata and exposes `response.fallbackInfo`.
sophia (product): Thanks all — happy path agreed. We'll reconvene on copy after RFC. :thumbsup:
